scope.resin: Separate guidance; do not apply FDM clearances directly to resin prints.
assumptions: Dimensions are starting values for calibration, not universal guarantees.
Print a small fit-test coupon before committing a large Split design.
All magnet and pin fits should be validated with the actual purchased hardware.

magnet_pockets.purpose: Provide repeatable magnetic closure or positioning while keeping magnets captive.

cylindrical_magnet.pocket_diameter: magnet_diameter + 0.25 mm for PLA; magnet_diameter + 0.30 mm for PETG
cylindrical_magnet.floor_thickness: at least 1.2 mm or 3 perimeters, whichever is greater

press_fit_alternative.caution: Use only after a coupon test; FDM holes and cylinders can vary by printer, orientation, and material.

design_rules: Model the pocket as a blind circular pocket with a flat floor; avoid relying on bridging for the magnet seat.
Add a 0.5 mm x 45 degree lead-in chamfer so the magnet enters cleanly and adhesive has room.
Leave 0.1-0.2 mm extra depth beyond magnet thickness so adhesive does not prevent full seating.
Orient the pocket so its opening faces upward or outward where practical; this avoids unsupported ceilings.
If the pocket ceiling must bridge, keep it short and use supports or redesign the orientation.
Lightly sand the magnet and pocket when using glue; this improves mechanical keying for adhesive.
Keep magnets away from thin walls and layer-splitting planes; embed them in solid, thick sections.
Use opposite-polarity pairs consistently and record orientation in the model filename or assembly notes.

pla_vs_petg.PLA: Start at +0.25 mm diameter and +0.15 mm depth for a glue fit; PLA generally needs slightly less clearance than PETG.
pla_vs_petg.PETG: Start at +0.30 mm diameter and +0.15 mm depth for a glue fit; increase by 0.05 mm if the magnet binds during a coupon test.

resin_notes: Resin parts are typically more dimensionally accurate than FDM parts, so use smaller clearances.
Start around +0.10 to +0.15 mm diameter for a glue-fit pocket and validate with the specific resin.
Ensure uncured resin can drain; avoid fully enclosed pockets unless drainage and curing are addressed.

dovetails.purpose: Provide a mechanical, self-aligning connection between two Split halves.
design_rules: Use a 60-degree included angle as a robust default; steeper angles resist separation but become harder to insert.
Apply clearance to both mating faces, not only one side; the starting values above are per side.
Add a 0.5 mm lead-in chamfer to the male feature and a matching entry relief to the female feature.
Avoid sharp internal corners; use at least a 0.5 mm fillet or radius where the model allows.
Keep the dovetail oriented to print with its sloped faces supported and avoid a large horizontal overhang.
Do not make the dovetail the sole structural load path for heavy or leveraged loads without testing.
For a removable connection, begin at the listed clearance; for a permanent glued assembly, reduce clearance only after coupon testing.

pla_vs_petg.PLA: Use 0.15 mm clearance per side as the first test; increase in 0.05 mm steps if assembly requires force.
pla_vs_petg.PETG: Use 0.20 mm clearance per side as the first test; PETG commonly needs a little more clearance for a non-binding fit.

resin_notes: Start with 0.10-0.15 mm total clearance for a snug resin dovetail, depending on resin and cure conditions.
Avoid very thin, sharp resin dovetails; they can be fragile and may not cure fully in deep narrow gaps.
Add drainage and cure access for any enclosed resin cavity.

alignment_pins.purpose: Positively locate Split halves before screws, magnets, adhesive, or dovetails carry the load.
design_rules: Use two alignment features: one round hole and one elongated slot when their centers are far apart.
The slot should point toward the other pin/hole so it absorbs printer and assembly misalignment.
Keep the slot at least 1.5 mm longer than the pin diameter as a practical starting value; increase it for larger parts.
Use a 4 mm pin diameter as a durable default for FDM; avoid small pins for structural alignment.
Provide at least 6 mm of engagement, but do not make the pin so long that assembly becomes difficult.
Add 0.5 mm x 45 degree chamfers to pins and holes to prevent catching during insertion.
Use pins for location; use screws, adhesive, magnets, or a dovetail for the primary retention and structural load.
Do not use three or more tightly toleranced pin/hole pairs; over-constraint causes binding.

pla_vs_petg.PLA: Start with a 4.20 mm hole for a 4.00 mm pin.
pla_vs_petg.PETG: Start with a 4.25 mm hole for a 4.00 mm pin.

resin_notes: Resin can resolve smaller features, but thin pins remain fragile.
Keep printed resin alignment pins at least 1 mm in diameter; prefer 2 mm or more for handling and durability.
Use slip fits rather than aggressive press fits unless the specific resin and printer have been calibrated.

validation.required_coupon: Print one coupon per material containing: a magnet pocket, a dovetail pair, and a pin/hole-plus-slot pair.

acceptance.magnet: Magnet seats fully with adhesive and does not protrude or sit loose.
acceptance.dovetail: Halves join by hand without binding and resist modest separation without permanent deformation.
acceptance.alignment_pins: Pins insert by hand or with light pressure; parts align without forcing.

validation.adjustment: Change one dimension at a time in 0.05 mm increments; do not change material, orientation, and clearance simultaneously.
